title: Projects for classification, surveillance and therapy in pediatric rheumatology
summary:
Children and adolescents with juvenile rheumatic diseases (juvenile idiopathic arthritis, JIA) require early and effective treatment to prevent long-term damage and maintain their quality of life. This project investigates how well these patients are currently being cared for and how their treatment can be improved.

The focus is on a treatment approach called “Treat to Target” (T2T). In this approach, physicians and patients define clear treatment goals together, such as the complete absence of disease activity. If this goal is not achieved within a specified period, the therapy is adjusted.

The researchers hypothesize that this structured approach increases the likelihood that children and adolescents will achieve long-term remission without the need for medication. At the same time, it may reduce long-term damage, improve quality of life, and lower healthcare costs.

To evaluate this, different groups of patients will be compared: those treated according to the T2T concept, as well as other groups based on current and historical data. Outcomes such as drug-free remission, quality of life, long-term damage, and healthcare costs will be assessed after at least three years.

In the long term, the project aims to promote a standardized approach to diagnosing and treating juvenile rheumatic diseases. The goal is to enable more effective and safer therapies, avoid unnecessary treatments, and provide the best possible care for affected children and adolescents.
